items.storyText:
Narrator: I'm making a special breakfast today: Granny's famous cinnamon buns.

Child narrator: To make the best buns, you need the best ingredients.

Narrator: I tell my sister Sam. So we hop on my bike and ride across town to Farmer Ray's.

Farmer Ray: You've come to the right place. My chickens lay wonderful eggs.

Narrator: The farmer says, pulling on his bushy beard. At the chicken coop, I gather two smooth brown eggs and a nervous chicken.

Farmer Ray: Cinnamon buns, you say? If it's butter you're after, you'll need to pack your bags. The best butter I know comes from Denmark.

Narrator: Farmer Ray smiles slyly. We all hop on his tractor, catch a plane, and watch as we zoom over the Atlantic Ocean. In Denmark, we head to rolling green fields, where we find an enormous sleepy cow. I introduce myself, my sister Sam, Farmer Ray, and the chicken to the cow's owner, explaining that my grandmother's cinnamon buns are not to be missed.

Farmer Lena: Well, you've come to the right place. My butter is the creamiest in the world. Cinnamon buns, you say? If it's flour you need, the heartiest wheat I know comes from France.

Narrator: Farmer Lena says, spilling some milk from a pail. We all ride the cow to the train to France, where we find an amber field of warm, dry grain and meet a French farmer who listens very closely to our plan.

Farmer François: Well, you've come to the right place. My wheat makes the very best flour in the entire world.

Narrator: Farmer François says, twirling his mustache. I grab two armfuls.

Farmer François: Cinnamon buns, you say? If it's vanilla you need, the finest vanilla in all the world comes from Madagascar. Come with me.

Narrator: We all hop in his hot-air balloon and set off over Africa, looking down on a magnificent leopard roaming the plains. In Madagascar, we march through the lush hills. There we meet Sabine, a vanilla grower, and I tell her the plan.

Farmer Sabine: Well, if you're making famous cinnamon buns, you've come to the right place. My vines produce the most fragrant vanilla beans in all the world.

Narrator: Farmer Sabine says, her eyes sparkling. I scoop up a handful of the heavy brown vanilla beans.

Farmer Sabine: Madagascar grows sugar cane and cinnamon, too. Let me take you to my friend Patrick's plantation.

Narrator: Patrick listens to the plan.

Patrick: True, I have the sweetest sugar cane and the very best cinnamon in the world. Sugar cane I can give you, but I'm afraid I can't help you with cinnamon. I'm all out. We harvested it yesterday.

Children: No cinnamon for the cinnamon buns? Now what?

Narrator: Something high atop a tree catches my eye: a small area of bark. I climb the tree and peel some off.

Child narrator: This will do!

Narrator: I say, grinning at the relieved crowd. We coax the cow and the chicken onto a steamship and head home before the ingredients spoil, mixing up a batch of Granny's famous cinnamon buns along the way.

Child narrator: Well?

Narrator: I ask as everyone chews and smiles.

Farmers: You were right! These are truly the very best cinnamon buns in all the world.

Child narrator: Now what should I make for lunch?
